articles.title: Fortnite Updates: December 14 Patch Unlocks Super Styles
articles.summary: The first update to Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 offers Super Level Styles, balance changes and more in preparation for this year’s Winterfest.
articles.body:
The first update to Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 has landed. With it comes weapon balance changes, Battle Pass goodies (namely Super Styles) and more in preparation for Fortnite’s Winterfest .

Fortnite Update: December 23 Update: Super Level Styles

In Fortnite, the desire to stand out amongst other players is strong. That said, so is the ability to look like your favorite character. How does one strut their stuff as Spider-Man and also maintain a somewhat unique flare? Simple. Super Level Styles .

Super Level Styles are bonus Battle Pass unlocks that alter the look of specific Chapter 3, Season 1 skins. Most of them were already available to players who hit level 100 of the pass. This update adds more, allowing anyone past level 140 to unlock rarer variations. These include a Photo Negative, Scarlet Blackout, and Gilded Reality versions of characters like Shanta and Lt. John Llama. Even Spider-Man got some new threads

Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 Balance Changes

Several weapons have been tweaked since this season started. A hotfix went out last week to address certain issues. This update offers more fine tuning. The Ranger Assault Rifle sports increased accuracy and damage. The Stinger SMG and Hunter Bolt Action Sniper both got animation tweaks to better showcase how much ammo they have when you’re reloading. The Striker Pump Shotgun , on the other hand, had its accuracy and rate of fire buffed. The Auto Shotgun also got a small buff. You’ll now be able to draw the weapon quicker than before.

Not all of Fortnite’s Season 3 weapons were buffed. Not only was the MK-Seven Assault Rifle’s environmental damage decreased, it’ll be less accurate when fired from the hip. This shouldn’t be shocking to most players; the MK is an incredibly powerful weapon in the right hands and that’s before considering its accuracy when aiming down sights.

Going beyond Fortnite’s weapons, the Guzzle Juice item’s heal speed has been increased.

What's Different About Fortnite Chapter 3

Recent events in Fortnite have ushered in sweeping changes to its island map. Fans can not only expect to see altered versions of familiar places, but there will be new locations as well, including Spider-Man/Peter Parker’s own Daily Bugle.

Marvel’s iconic newspaper facility won’t be the only new area worth exploring, as The Sanctuary, The Seven’s secret base of operations, has been revealed as well.

Beyond new characters and map changes, Fortnite Chapter 3 adds new traversal mechanics. These include the ability to slide about in hopes of evading enemy fire or the new swinging mechanic that allows you to mimic Spidey’s movements.

Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 also introduces the biggest game-changing feature since Reboot Vans in Camps. These special locations will allow you and your squadmates to store items to be used in later matches. Not only that, it’ll also allow you heal up after taking damage.

Fans can expect new items and weapons scattered all over the island. If utilized well (and with a bit luck) they’ll be able to get multiple Victory Royales and potentially earn the new Victory Crown. This digital accolade will certainly encourage competitive play.

Fortnite: Chapter 3, Season 1 Battle Pass

It wouldn’t be a new season of Fortnite without a brand-new Battle Pass. This latest pass will offer a lot of the same – new skins, emotes, weapon wraps, etc. It also features the amazing Spider-Man. While those things are worth getting excited for, it’s Epic Games allowing players to continue earning Battle Pass XP outside of Battle Royale that’s really interesting.

Done by using the Accolade Device, Fortnite Creative Mode players can build XP gain into their created experiences. They won’t be able to set the amount, so it won't be easy for players to blast through all 100 levels. Instead, they can set XP award weight based on the number Accolade Devices they have and how frequent players are awarded.

Essentially, players won’t be able to manually type in how much XP they want their friends to earn. All of the math is done in the background in a way that keeps things balanced; players will be able to influence things based on the complexity of their created accolades but won’t be able to give out free XP.

This update comes with the usual bug fixes. What’s exciting is that these changes weren’t just to improve Fortnite but also to make way for this year’s Winterfest event. There’s been no word on what day it’ll launch, besides soon. One should expect new missions, seasonal items and more in the coming days though.

And that’s it for Fortnite’s latest update. Be sure to check back here for more Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 patch notes! Also, if you missed it or want to make sure you didn't miss a thing, read our breakdown of Fortnite Chapter 2's finale event and the introduction of The Rock as The Foundation.

Kenneth Seward Jr. is a freelance writer, editor, and illustrator who covers games, movies, and more. Follow him @kennyufg and on Twitch.

articles.title: Celebrate The Legend of Zelda on Switch 2 With IGN Guides
articles.body:
To celebrate the release of Nintendo Switch 2 – and the 19(!) different Zelda games that are now playable on the system – the IGN Guides team has made a few upgrades to ensure you'll have a helping hand when you most need it. Not everyone needs a walkthrough to get to the end, but we hope these new features and upgrades can inspire even the most seasoned Zelda player to return and discover something they may have missed or skipped on a previous playthrough.

Speaking of smooth sailing, we hope you’re as excited as we are to revisit one of GameCube’s best games, The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker in its original form. Yes, that means the slow-sailing and long Triforce Chart/Shard quest found in the OG version are back – and you may want to use our guide to make sure you don’t head in the wrong direction. Our Wind Waker guide was originally written in 2002, but we’ve worked on some big upgrades to make it nice and new for Switch 2! Here’s what you can expect:

The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker Guide and Map

We have overhauled our guide and walkthrough with new high-resolution screenshots, added in-page tracking, checklists, new videos, and radically upgraded our interactive map. Instead of just showing you a desktop or mobile version of the in-game map, we have redone it from the ground up and you can now zoom in all the way and see every island, enemy platform, and submarine up close. Track which Pieces of Heart , charts , and items you’ve collected and start chasing all 135 Nintendo Gallery images to finally get that 100% completion. If you prefer video, you can even track every Treasure Chart via in-video checklists (or jump to the exact spot in the video from the guide). The guide and videos of course also address the Wii U HD vs GameCube/Switch 2 version differences so that it all works for both versions.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild Guide and Map

Nintendo’s biggest-ever series reboot arrived on Switch 2 with upgraded framerate and resolution. If you’re like us and you’re itching to go back and see how it plays after sinking hundreds of hours into Tears of the Kingdom, we’ve got you. As a thank you to our returning IGN Guides users, our tracking experience will be completely free for the next three months, giving you enough time to finally find and check off every Korok Seed . Each seed location comes with brief hints for those who want to figure out things on their own – or you can click through to the guide for detailed tips if you're stumped.

Here are the most popular pages for people trying to 100% the game:

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom Guide and Map

We’ve updated our Tears of the Kingdom guide and map to get ready for the Switch 2 re-release as well. While Nintendo hasn’t changed a ton over the original Switch release, there are some updates we’ve detailed in our guide. If you’re jumping back in to finally complete the main quest, you can start with our detailed walkthrough , or embark on the never-ending Korok hunt and track everything on our Interactive Map .

If you’re wondering what changed and need some pointers for the new Switch 2-specific features, check out these links:

The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past Guide and Map

Surprise! We quietly snuck out an update to our classic A Link to the Past guide a few weeks ago – if you’ve never played or finished this 2D openworld gem, you could do worse than playing it via Nintendo Switch Online on either Switch console. It might not have the hundreds of collectibles of its 3D successors, but there are plenty of things to discover on Link to the Past ’s dual map.

We may be a little LTTP (sorry) – but we figured “better late than never” and rolled out a complete interactive map that lets you track every Piece of Heart and discover every cave and secret hidden in the 1991 classic. We also added checklists and all-new screenshots throughout the guide to make it all shiny and new!

The Legend of Zelda: Links Awakening Guide and Map

Launched on Nintendo Switch in 2019, Link's Awakening has finally gotten the update we've all been asking for: a smooth framerate. Play it on Switch 2 and you'll be able to experience Link's most-charming adventure in a dreamy 60fps at 4K resolution. Our guide helps you get to 100% completion, including all Pieces of Heart . If you used our guide way back when, check out this cool upgrade we made to the videos featured in the guide:

You can check off the collectible figures you've collected via the on-screen checklist trackers while watching the video in embed mode.

You can also bring up the in-video checklist by clicking on the button in the lower-right corner.

The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom Guide and Map

Players have made extensive use of our Echoes checklists -- and we can tell you that the Rock, the Table, and the Zol Echo are the most collected Echoes overall. But we were also shocked that so many players who played Echoes of Wisdom outright skipped Dampe's Automaton side quest ! With the upgraded resolution and framerate on Switch 2, you may want to take another look and get all six mechanical helpers. We made it easy by providing a handy table that you can sort and filter.

Beyond these select Zelda games and guides that received upgrades this month, there is of course plenty more Zelda to be found on Nintendo Switch 2. Whether it's the Hyrule Warriors spin-offs, Skyward Sword, the NES, Game Boy Color, and Advance classics, or our two 64-bit favorites, IGN Guides has you covered. And if enough people find our Link to the Past and Wind Waker maps helpful, maybe we'll give some of those guides some upgrades as well.

Peer Schneider originally launched IGN Guides in 1999 and is now heading up IGN Entertainment's guides, tools, and game assist teams across IGN, Map Genie, Maxroll, and Gamer Network.

articles.title: Sony’s first clip earbuds don’t quite hit the mark
articles.summary: While they’re comfortable and have good sound performance (for an open earbud), the Sony LinkBuds Clip are light on features for the price.
articles.body: The Sony LinkBuds Clip are the company’s first clip earbuds. They follow the innovative donut-hole LinkBuds and LinkBuds Open and, like their predecessors, allow you to listen to music or podcasts, make phone calls, or be active outdoors while still maintaining awareness of your surroundings. The clip design has become more popular over the past couple of years, and while the LinkBuds Clip have a solid design and good sound, there’s nothing significant that sets them apart from competitors, especially at their $229.99 price. Like other open earbuds, the LinkBuds Clip wrap around your ear helix like an ear cuff. The small spherical speaker enclosure is positioned just outside your ear canal and is connected by a flexible band to a larger capsule-shaped housing that rests on the outside. I like the look of the Clip buds, with their slightly glossy enclosures and selection of subdued color tones, including lavender, green, greige (a grayish beige), and black. Some might prefer a bolder, flashier look, but I like the green sample Sony provided. You can also mix and match five different case covers — black, green, blue, coral, and lavender — to customize them. [Product: Sony LinkBuds Clip | The Clip are intended to sit midway up your ear, but since everyone’s ears are different, there could be some adjustment to find the most comfortable spot for you (for me, it’s a little lower on my ear). Once you find the sweet spot, putting the earbuds on is quick and easy, although I found the fit a bit loose. The band isn’t as flexible as the one on the Shokz OpenDots One, which fit more securely around my ear. Instead, Sony includes silicone “cushions” that fit around the band. (Color-matching cushions come with the additional top case covers.) They gave me the secure fit I was looking for, and I was able to wear them for nearly an entire workday without discomfort. I even forgot I was wearing them at times, since they let in ambient sound. Those with larger ears might feel more of a pinch from them, even without the cushions attached. [Image: The Clip earbuds fit around the ear’s helix, with the speaker sitting outside of the ear canal. The highs and lows of the Clip’s sound performance While I preferred the fit of the LinkBuds Clip with the cushions, using them affected the sound balance. The cushions caused the speakers to sit just a bit farther away from my ear canal, which resulted in less bass performance. And the Clip — and really every pair of open earbuds — are a bit light on thumping bass. There are three primary listening modes: standard, voice boost, and sound leakage reduction. Standard mode sounds the most natural, with a clear midrange that doesn’t overpower the higher frequencies. Voice boost added a bit too much vocal presence that became oppressive over longer music listening sessions, but added good clarity for podcasts and news programs. The sound leakage reduction mode cuts out much of the high-end response, limiting potential disturbances to those around you, but it also makes the music sound muffled and dull. And there wasn’t a significant amount of leakage anyway, even in standard and voice boost modes. [Image: The LinkBuds have a USB-C charging port, but do not support wireless charging. There are some presets in Sony’s Sound Connect app, as well as a 10-band equalizer, if you want to boost or cut a specific frequency range. For some of my more rocking tracks — Soundgarden’s “Spoonman,” for instance — I pumped up the bass and low mids a bit. There’s also Sony’s DSEE, which improves the sound of compressed audio a little bit. The LinkBuds Clip really shine when on calls. They have a new AI noise-reduction chip and bone-conduction sensor that allow them to focus on the wearer’s voice and isolate it from the noise around them. During multiple calls while walking down the busier streets in my Los Angeles neighborhood, my friends could easily hear me, while the traffic around me was suppressed. There were occasional moments where they commented about hearing a gust of wind or the sirens of a nearby police car, but they were fleeting. It was during those moments, though, that I had some trouble hearing them because of the Clip’s open design. A bit lean on features I was a bit surprised at some of what was missing with the LinkBuds Clip, especially for $230. While they have good battery life at nine hours per charge (and another 28 hours with the case), the case doesn’t have wireless charging. The earbuds support the standard SBC and AAC codecs, but Sony’s own high-res LDAC is missing. They also don’t have audio sharing, which is available on the WF-1000XM5 and can now be found for only $25 more than the Clip. The touch controls can be finicky. You use multiple taps for different controls — two taps on the right side to pause and play, three taps for the next song, and four taps to raise the volume (or lower the volume on the left earbuds). But the spot to tap on the band has a small margin of error, so if my finger was off target at all, the taps wouldn’t register. It was even harder while jogging. I’d need to slow down to a fast walk to get better control. [Image: [Image: You can set up scene-based listening in the Sound Connect app, which allows you to customize the earbuds’ functionality based on your activity or location. So you can have a specific playlist start when you start running, or when you arrive home, the app can switch to your favorite music streaming service. You can also have the app read out notifications in your ear. It’s an interesting feature if you have certain routines and invest in the time to set it up. It makes sense that Sony came out with the Clip, especially since it helped popularize the open earbuds trend with the original LinkBuds. And the Clip are good earbuds that look cool, sound pretty good, and are comfortable. But for $230, there’s nothing that sets them apart from other recent open earbuds like the Shokz OpenDots One and EarFun Clip, both of which are cheaper. Once they come down in price or go on sale, they’ll be much more of an enticing purchase. But until then, unless you’re in love with the LinkBuds Clip look, it’s better to wait. Photography by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

articles.title: Was Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton Really That Bad? Has Brock Lesnar Actually Retired After Losing to Oba Femi? Here's our full review of WrestleMania 42.
articles.summary: A fantastic, star-studded Night Two saves WrestleMania 42 after a dull and confusing Night One.
articles.body:
A weekend of two halves, wasn't it? Night One of WrestleMania 42 underwhelmed as much as it confused, but come Roman Reigns’ final spear of CM Punk on Sunday, the feelings couldn't have been any different. And that's ultimately what a main event at WrestleMania should be aiming to achieve — a satisfying, cleanly delivered ending to a story. Where Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton's clash came across as a largely muddled series of spots trying to untie an overly complicated knot that had taken weeks to tie itself tighter, Night Two's headline attraction was exactly what it needed to be — a fantastic wrestling match between two of the best to ever do it.

But of course, WrestleMania isn't only about the main events, and with 13 matches (plus one highly enjoyable Danhausen interlude) to sift through, let’s get stuck right in. Starting with the positives, let's head straight to Night Two, in which every one of the matchups was great at the very least. Oba Femi's WrestleMania debut was everything we hoped it to be, and his march down the Allegiant Stadium ramp produced a louder noise from the crowd than was heard at any point during the night before. Watching two powerhouses go toe-to-toe was always going to be a treat, and The Ruler's swift dispatching of Brock Lesnar with his already signature Fall from Grace felt like a true changing of the guard moment. On a stage where Lesnar had brutalised many opponents, Oba confirmed what we already knew — he's the fastest rising star in WWE and well on his way to being its biggest attraction.

What we didn't see coming was Brock's instant reaction to such a convincing defeat, as he lay flat on the Las Vegas mat before slowly taking off his equipment. It felt more like a farewell to WrestleMania for The Beast than to WWE as a whole, with a retirement surely far more likely to be sealed via a Gunther submission, but it was certainly an uncharacteristic show of emotion from Lesnar. Whether you think he should be in the spotlight, given the details alleged in the ongoing Vince McMahon court case, is a valid concern. I’d be lying if I said I was at all fully comfortable enjoying him returning to the ring under such a cloud, but it would appear you'd have a hard time telling the WrestleMania 42 crowd that. There was an outpouring that swelled upon his embrace with long-time advocate Paul Heyman that secured both an expected and unexpected opening to a stacked Night Two card. If this is the last time we ever see Brock Lesnar, you certainly won't find me crying, though.

What followed was pure fun, and the perfect palette cleanser as the six-man ladder match for the Intercontinental Championship provided awesome acrobatics and painful landings in equal measure. Entrance highlights included Penta's Shao Kahn mask from Mortal Kombat and fellow luchador Dragon Lee's expansive, reptilian wings — not that you would've seen that on TV, thanks to one of many frequently ill-timed ad breaks. Everyone involved had a fun spot to take home with them, with JD McDonagh and Rusev taking the lion's share of the punishment. Rusev, in particular, ended up on the wrong end of a Je'Von Evans OG Cutter, launched from the ring post before catching the bulky Bulgarian from the top rung of the ladder – perhaps providing the match's biggest “wow” moment. In truth, it was a match full of big spots fuelled by impressive athleticism, timing, and choreography, even if Penta's eventual retention of the belt didn't carry much tension in its final moments.

The crowd-pleasing didn't stop there, either. The sheer volume of the “Whoop that Trick” chants would place most wrestlers on the back foot, and in truth, Sami Zayn had no real chance of ever winning them over as he slid further into heel territory, which was all but confirmed as Sad Sami returned and he sat slumped against the announcement table following Trick's capture of the US Championship belt. The win-sealing Trick shot and subsequent celebrations felt like another of 42's baton-passing moments, as Williams followed up Oba and Je'Von's impressive showings as the next generation of WWE stars made their mark on the biggest stage.

While new talent is exciting, sometimes returning heroes are just as fun. Whether you'd class the Demon as a hero is certainly up to you, but I, for one, couldn't have been happier to see Finn Balor's twisted creation snarl and crawl his way onto the mat to face a terrified-looking Dominik Mysterio. As with the previous match, the in-ring action wasn't the peak of the night's offerings, but a good ol’ fashioned dose of revenge was dealt out in an impromptu street fight, sealed with a Demon Coup de Grace through both Dirty Dom and a Slim Jim table. Balor still very much has the technical ability, but Mysterio still has a little to learn in this regard, and one gets the feeling he will need to continue to improve if he ever harbours genuine main event aspirations. But, he's still young and certainly has the character side of the business nailed already. The Demon was always going to be the main draw here, and he played his role perfectly. I can't wait to see where both of them go next as the Judgment Day continues to be a concept of yesteryear.

Speaking of which, you'll struggle to find a superstar carrying as much aura as Rhea Ripley. Her tussle with Jade Cargill continued Night Two's hot streak to great effect, as the two powerhouses seemed well matched for each other —- something both have historically struggled with due to their imposing physiques in the women's division. Cargill had her moments, namely the unveiling of a new Kenny Omega-inspired slam, but, again, you always felt this one was destined to end with the belt in Ripley's hands. Rhea holding it aloft as she celebrated with her teammate and best friend, Iyo Sky, will go down as one of the enduring images of WrestleMania 42, and even slightly softens the blow of the Genius of the Sky not getting her own match in Vegas. A crime if you ask me.

And so the stage was set for hatred to fill the ring. Roman Reigns began ceremonies with a stoic tribute to his bloodline, soundtracked by the return of his old Head of the Table theme music. CM Punk replied in suit, as his old theme, AFI's Miseria Cantare, played behind clips of his entire WWE career, before launching into his current Cult of Personality entrance that the crowd echoed in chorus. It takes a lot for a WrestleMania crowd to be split entirely down the middle, but that's what the loud Las Vegas audience pretty much sounded like. The action fit the occasion, too. There were some fun move-stealing shenanigans and announcer table-breaking splashes peppered among the highlights of the 30-minute brawl, all before Roman claimed an exhausting win. Could it be that his barb targeting Punk's age a couple of weeks back proved true as the future hall of famer appeared to run out of gas after many near falls?

It was a fantastic main event, carrying all the ingredients that you'd want: history, drama, and a clean finish to a story. It's exactly what Randy Orton vs. Cody Rhodes should have been, who have more history between them than most active wrestlers. And that's ultimately what made Saturday's main event so frustrating. That's not to say there weren't great moments. In fact, much of the action was enjoyable, with, again, a fair share of move-stealing going on throughout. But by the time what felt like the 28th RKO had been delivered, my main feeling was confusion.

Why did Pat McAfee have to come back only to deliver a fair count as a heel ref? Why did Orton turn on him after saying he wanted him there so badly just 24 hours earlier? Why did he also RKO poor Charles Robinson? Why was Rhodes also playing the heel only for Orton to upstage him? Why did Orton punt Cody after he had lost instead of doing it in the match? Why did Orton, once again, hold up a belt he didn't win?

So many questions without logical answers, which pretty much summed up this storyline ever since Randy first picked up that phone. What could have been a simple but effective story about a mentor and an apprentice lost its way rapidly to the point where I'm not even sure the WWE creative team knew the tale they wanted to tell. You can't blame the performers. Randy was vicious, and Cody responded to the crowd's boos without turning fully heel. Even Jelly Roll hit a pretty good splash into McAfee, which everyone enjoyed. But if you've left me feeling unclear in my emotions following the end of the match, then you've failed in your storytelling.

At least I did feel something, because much of Night One left me cold. Well, as much as you can be in the Mojave Desert. The card was rattled through with matches rarely passing 10 minutes in length and, I'm told, packed full of commercials (I didn't get a sense of this from inside the stadium, I'm afraid). IShowSpeed flipping onto Logan Paul was enjoyable, as was Jacob taking the entire contents of a toolbox to Drew McIntyre. But these fights barely had time for more than one semi-memorable moment apiece. I'll always enjoy Becky Lynch's work, but her win over AJ Lee won't live long in the memory. Paige's return was certainly exciting, but we all know that she and Brie Bella won't be holding those tag titles for long, so I ended up just feeling sorry for Bayley, who has been denied a WrestleMania moment once again. Then there's Liv Morgan's match with Stephanie Vaquer, which felt like it was over before it began.

The one saving grace was Seth Rollins’ battle with Gunther. There was never a doubt in my mind that such fantastic in-ring workers would deliver — and they did. The giant Austrian managed to further assert his dominance, but time was still given to create legitimate jeopardy for him. Rollins’ superplex into a Falcon Arrow was perhaps the most impressive move of the whole evening, and if it wasn't for a returning Bron Breakker, he very well could have taken it. The ramp-long sprint into the spear from the member of The Vision was the real cherry on top of this one, as the crowd barked loudly in response.

articles.title: Final Fantasy VII’s remake trilogy will conclude with Revelation
articles.summary: Square Enix has shared details about the third game in the FFVII trilogy.
articles.body: Square Enix has officially announced the third and final game in its Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy: Final Fantasy VII Revelation. It will release on multiple platforms simultaneously — PC, PS5, Xbox Series X / S, and Nintendo Switch 2 — in spring 2027. In footage shown onstage at Summer Game Fest Live, there was a lot to take in: You’ll get to fly the Highwind airship, jump off it to land in the game’s open world, play as Vincent Valentine and Cid Highwind in battle (who weren’t playable in Rebirth), challenge the gigantic Weapons, and visit places from the original game, like Wutai. You’ll also get to dress up your characters with armors that have special movesets, in what’s actually called the “FITS” system (“Function Integrated Tactical Suitwear”) — it’s intended to be like a jobs system from classic Final Fantasy games. In one trailer, you can get a closer look at things like the game’s world, which Vincent Valentine voice actor Matt Mercer says is “our most expansive open world yet” and one where you can “pick a direction and set sail.” It sounds as if you’ll have the agency to basically go wherever you want: “Where will the winds guide you first? That freedom is in your hands.” [Media: And here is Square Enix’s official description of the game, from the trailer at the top of this post: > As the world teeters on the brink of annihilation, the final battle against Sephiroth begins. A meteor mars the sky, monstrous planetary guardians wreak havoc across the globe, and the fires of war rage. Now, Cloud and his companions must stand against this chaos to not only decide the planet’s fate, but bring a legendary conflict to its conclusion. > In the final chapter of the FINAL FANTASY VII remake project, the scale has never been larger and the stakes have never been higher. Take to the skies and explore a boundless world, fight alongside a fully assembled party, master strategic and dynamic combat, and prepare yourself for the climactic finale. > A vast planet awaits. Everything leads here. Revelation will conclude a yearslong saga that, so far, has actually turned out pretty well. Final Fantasy VII Remake was a thrilling, thoughtful take on the original that focused on the Midgar portion of the FFVII story. Four years later, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth let Cloud Strife and friends explore a big open world and also added the excellent Queen’s Blood in-game card game. (If you have save data from the upgraded Remake Intergrade or Rebirth, you’ll get bonus summon Materia in Revelation, according to Square Enix.) Oh, and one detail that fans of the remake trilogy may or may not be happy about for the third game in the series: Chadley, the strange, humanlike cyborg, will be back.

articles.title: The Switch 2’s VRR update doesn’t extend to third-party docks, it seems.
articles.summary:
After installing the recent version 23.0.0 update on my Nintendo Switch 2, I can’t access the VRR settings option while it’s plugged into the Jsaux OmniCentro dock (I haven’t tried Genki’s Covert Dock 3 yet). The good news is that this dock still works post-update, but the ball is in third-party makers’ court to deliver a patch that enables VRR.

articles.title: Nintendo Announces New Switch Sale Made Possible By "Tariff-Related" Refunds
articles.summary: Nintendo announces a 30% off Customer Appreciation Sale for Switch games and accessories, funded in part by tariff refunds following recent US litigation.
articles.body:
Nintendo has announced a new 'Customer Appreciation' Sale in the U.S, offering 30% off dozens of Switch games and more, starting on September 13 and running through September 26.

Select games, downloadable content, accessories, amiibo, and apparel will be discounted, although Nintendo has not yet provided a full list of the games and other products that will be included in the sale across the Nintendo eShop, Nintendo Store, and other participating retailers.

The video game giant has also said that the promotion is "made possible in part by tariff-related refunds" . The company says it "absorbed most tariff-related costs", but the refunds have helped make promotions such as this new sale possible.

Nintendo previously faced questions over what it would do with money returned after the US tariff regime was challenged. Nintendo recently raised the prices of some Switch products globally, citing a combination of factors including tariffs, rising component costs, labour and shipping.

It subsequently argued that consumers were not entitled to refunds for purchases made at those higher prices after a court ruled the tariffs illegal. Nintendo said customers had received "exactly what they bargained and paid for" and that it was not required to retroactively adjust prices following the outcome of the tariff litigation.

Nintendo also maintained that it had absorbed the tariff costs on the Switch 2 itself rather than simply passing them directly on to consumers.

Now, however, Nintendo says tariff-related refunds have helped make its latest promotion possible. The company says it absorbed most of the tariff-related costs, while the refunds have contributed towards promotions such as the new Customer Appreciation Sale.

But it's already been a fairly big week for Nintendo fans/ With the two Nintendo Directs back to back , preorders for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Metroid Ravenous going live , as well as that elusive 40th Anniversary Zelda Switch 2 announcement.

Nintendo has also just released a fresh firmware update for its Switch and Switch 2 consoles , including adding VRR support while playing Switch 2 in TV mode.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides . As a massive Doctor Who fan, he also keeps a close eye on physical media deals like Doctor Who Blu-ray preorders , and occasionally steps away from commerce to contribute reviews for the site, such as his review of Doctor Who's latest season .

articles.title: 'You Get Your Tariff Money back... if You Give Them More Money' — Fans React to Nintendo's 'Customer Appreciation' Sale
articles.summary: Fans are reacting to the announcement of a unique "Customer Appreciation" sale that Nintendo claims has been "made possible in part by tariff-related refunds."
articles.body:
Fans are reacting to the announcement of a unique "Customer Appreciation" sale that Nintendo claims has been "made possible in part by tariff-related refunds."

Nintendo will temporarily reduce the price of "dozens of Nintendo Switch digital games and bundles, plus savings on select physical games, downloadable content, accessories, amiibo and apparel." Whether Nintendo Switch 2 games will also be included is unknown.

While cheaper prices are nothing to be sniffed at, the framing of this promotion — which runs for just two weeks, from September 13 through September 26 — as being funded by tariff refunds has certainly raised eyebrows.

Nintendo and numerous other companies are now recouping the money they previously handed over to the U.S. government as part of tariffs that have since been deemed illegal. Nintendo (and again, numerous other companies) raised prices to combat these tariffs , and fans have been calling for Nintendo to pass some of its tariff refund back to gamers. Indeed, a proposed class action lawsuit is brewing, calling for Nintendo to share its refund with Switch purchasers — but the company itself has argued that it has no reason to do so .

Today's sale announcement is being taken by some fans as a way to placate those fans who remain upset about all this, while also continuing to signal that it won't be doling out partial refunds to any recent Switch and Switch 2 customers.

While the lack of partial refunds isn't particularly surprising, what is rather remarkable here is the acknowledgement that Nintendo did very well out of the whole situation — to the extent that it is now lowering prices (by a small amount, on a selection of titles, for a limited time).

"Ah yes, because they couldn't have possibly had a sale if it wasn't for the tariffs," wrote one fan on video game forum ResetEra .

"It's a coupon. Makes them look good and gets people to spend money. Win-win for them," wrote another.

"Lol the gall of them," wrote a third. "'We'll do a sale to celebrate not giving your money back.'"

"Nintendo is f***ing allergic to any percentage higher than 30%," wrote yet another fan. "Still, the fact that they're offering a discount at all as some sort of 'apology' is surprising in itself."

Nintendo is yet to reveal exactly which games and other products will be part of the sale, and we may not find out until the price reductions go live on September 13. But even despite the scepticism, there are plenty of fans who have already expressed excitement for the sale, and who sound ready to splash out further.

"So you get your tariff money back... if you give them more money," concluded one fan. "You know what? I'll take it lol."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: GTA 4 Was the Xbox 360’s ‘We Mean Business’ Moment Against the PS3
articles.summary: I’d argue that GTA 4’s simultaneous release on Xbox 360 and subsequent exclusive DLC might’ve been where the Xbox brand peaked from a cultural perspective. You had to have an Xbox 360 – if not for the killer lineup of games it already had, then for the exclusive GTA 4 expansions. It was right up there with the release of Halo 3 in 2007. In fact, Fall of 2007 – which saw the release of Halo 3, Mass Effect, BioShock, Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, Rock Band, and Assassin’s Creed – through GTA 4’s release in April of 2008 might be the best six-or-so-month run any console has ever had.
articles.body:
This is an IGN opinion piece from Ryan McCaffrey, who worked at Official Xbox Magazine from 2002-2012 during the original Xbox and Xbox 360 era before joining IGN, where he remains “the Xbox guy.” In the run-up to Xbox’s 25th anniversary, he’ll be sharing his memories from the platform’s first quarter-century.

As the hugely anticipated release of GTA 6 is now just over two months away, it’s worth remembering how it wasn’t so long ago that the Grand Theft Auto games were PlayStation exclusives. GTA 3 and Vice City didn’t see the light of day on the original Xbox until November of 2003 when the pair shipped as the GTA Double Pack, meaning that GTA 3 was exclusive to PS2 for two years and Vice City for one. San Andreas, meanwhile, hit Xbox in June of 2005, a comparatively short eight months after its initial PS2 release.

The point is, when then-Head of Xbox Peter Moore – easily the best showman that’s ever run the Xbox business – rolled up his sleeve to reveal a “tattoo” of the Grand Theft Auto IV logo on his bicep at E3 2006 and announce that not only would Rockstar’s next-gen GTA ship day-and-date on the Xbox 360, but that Xbox would get not one but two timed-exclusive expansion packs (which later turned out to be the excellent The Lost and Damned and the absolutely sublime The Ballad of Gay Tony), it was the biggest of big deals. Microsoft cut Rockstar a $50 million check for the privilege, but it was worth it. At least to Xbox 360 gamers, many of whom had invested in Microsoft’s first-to-market HD Era next-gen console after its incredibly strong out-of-the-gate showing with games like Call of Duty 2 , The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion , Ghost Recon Advanced Warfighter, and Fight Night Round 3 all being verified next-gen powerhouses before the E3 2006 Xbox press conference – and before the PS3 even shipped.

Microsoft had gotten off to a huge start (as Moore used to say, “The first one to 10 million wins”), and with this GTA 4 deal, the company had shown that it was standing behind the millions of gamers who had “jumped in” with the Xbox 360 in its early days. Xbox 360 gamers wouldn’t be second-class citizens when it came to the industry’s biggest franchise.

And when GTA 4 finally got released in April of 2008 (after a delay from Fall 2007), it was, of course, a from-the-ground-up masterpiece that shared nothing in common, technologically speaking, with the GTA 3 trilogy. It took us back to Liberty City, albeit a completely reimagined one that looked incredible and was packed with small details and stuff to do. It is, in my humble opinion, the funniest of all of the satirically brilliant GTA games, as it featured the hilarious in-game internet (accessible at internet cafes…remember those?), memorable characters like Brucie, and laugh-out-loud in-universe TV shows like “The Men’s Room.”

Speaking very personally, it also came out very shortly after I got divorced, and I have really meaningful memories of my best friend Robert flying up from Arizona right after it came out to keep me company and enjoy the game with me. There was no GTA Online back then, of course, so we’d just pass the controller back and forth, each reveling in (and laughing along with) the crazy antics of the person with the gamepad in their hand. We must’ve put a few dozen hours into GTA 4 in the few days he stayed with me, and I’ll always associate GTA 4 with a much-needed bit of fun and levity and friendship in a moment when I needed it most.

Later, as I mentioned, The Lost and the Damned dropped (and stayed exclusive to Xbox for over a year), and its focus on the biker gang of the same name was a super cool pivot on the typical GTA formula. And later still, The Ballad of Gay Tony (a six-month Xbox 360 exclusive) featured impeccable storytelling and character work by Rockstar; heck, I’d personally rank it among the best DLCs or expansions for any game, ever. And then at the tail end of the Xbox 360 generation we got GTA 5…though sadly no single-player DLC at all, as originally promised, let alone exclusive DLC.

Anyway, I’d argue that GTA 4’s simultaneous release on Xbox 360 and subsequent exclusive DLC might’ve been where the Xbox brand peaked from a cultural perspective. You had to have an Xbox 360 – if not for the killer lineup of games it already had, then for the exclusive GTA 4 expansions. It was right up there with the release of Halo 3 in 2007. In fact, Fall of 2007 – which saw the release of Halo 3, Mass Effect, BioShock, Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, Rock Band, and Assassin’s Creed – through GTA 4’s release in April of 2008 might be the best six-or-so-month run any console has ever had.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Professor Layton and the Curious Village Remake Announced, Coming to Multiple Platforms in 2027
articles.summary: A Professor Layton and the Curious Village remake has been announced by series developer Level-5.
articles.body:
A Professor Layton and the Curious Village remake has been announced by series developer Level-5.

Revealed today during the Level-5 Vision 2026 Showcase, this fresh version of the classic puzzle game will arrive at some point in 2027 for Nintendo Switch, Switch 2, PC via Steam and PlayStation 5.

A press release notes that the remake's characters have been reimagined in 3D, while the world of St. Mystere has been made more immersive with greater depth and richer detail. Professor Layton and the Curious Village's animated cutscenes have also been given a lick of paint, with higher resolution and widescreen formatting.

🆕 Annonce – Professeur Layton et l’étrange village Remake sortira sur Nintendo Switch 2 et Nintendo Switch en 2027, découvrez la première bande-annonce du jeu. pic.twitter.com/cuhbyIpMbH — NintendHOME – News & Opinions Nintendo (@NintendHOME) September 10, 2026

🆕 Annonce – Professeur Layton et l’étrange village Remake sortira sur Nintendo Switch 2 et Nintendo Switch en 2027, découvrez la première bande-annonce du jeu. pic.twitter.com/cuhbyIpMbH

Next year will mark the 20th anniversary of Professor Layton and the Curious Village's original release back on Nintendo DS, kickstarting a series that now extends to two trilogies of games featuring Professor Hershel Layton and his apprentice Luke Triton, plus further spinoffs and a memorable crossover with Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney.

An all-new Professor Layton game is also on the way, of course: Professor Layton and the New World of Steam , which is set to launch for Switch, Switch, PC and PS5 on December 10.

Professor Layton and the New World of Steam Level 5 Vision Trailer Stills

Will further remakes follow? That may depend on how well Professor Layton and the Curious Village performs. But for anyone wanting to see how the series started on modern hardware, this remake may end up well worth a look.

articles.title: This Avengers: Doomsday Figure Reveals a Closer Look at Doctor Doom's Alternate Costume
articles.summary: Robert Downey, Jr.'s Doctor Doom will wear at least two costumes in Avengers: Doomsday, and a new action figure gives us a much better look at his alternate suit of armor.
articles.body:
Robert Downey, Jr.'s Iron Man rarely stuck to just one suit of armor in his many MCU appearances, and it appears that the same will hold true for Downey's new character, Doctor Doom. Doom will wear at least two distinct suits of armor in Avengers: Doomsday , and now we've gotten a much better look at his secondary costume thanks to a new Hot Toys figure.

Having already revealed their standard Doctor Doom figure , Hot Toys and Sideshow Collectibles have now debuted the companion Victor von Doom figure. Get a closer look in the slideshow gallery below:

Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday Victor von Doom Figure

While this armor follows the same traditional Doom design aesthetic (green cloak and metal mask), it's quite a bit different from the other Doom suit seen in the film. It seems to be less an actual suit of armor and more a piece of regal formal wear. The green suit is more muted in color and completely covers up the armored components here. The mask is also completely different - smoother and less aggressive than the one on the Doctor Doom armor.

This suit appears to be the same one Downey's character was wearing during his initial appearance in the post-credits scene of The Fantastic Four: First Steps . Our best guess is that Doom will wear this suit in the early portions of Avengers: Doomsday, before his true power and motivations are made clear to Earth's Mightiest Heroes.

Sideshow hasn't yet put the Victor von Doom figure up for preorder. But if the Doctor Doom figure is any indication, we'd expect it to cost around $285 and release in late 2027.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18. Fans can get an early tease for the movie in the form of Avengers: Endgame Encore, which is set to be the longest MCU movie to date . Marvel also teased Doomsday by recreating the trailer in LEGO form .

articles.title: GTA 6's Limited Edition PS5 Controller Pre-Orders Overload PlayStation's Store, and Scalpers Are Already Reselling Them on eBay
articles.summary: Pre-orders went live for Grand Theft Auto 6's new PS5 controllers this morning and the experience was extremely chaotic.
articles.body:
Pre-orders went live for Grand Theft Auto 6's new PS5 controllers this morning, and the experience was extremely chaotic.

As you might expect, there's a ravenous demand for anything related to GTA 6. When Sony announced that they'd be opening up pre-orders for a pair of limited edition GTA 6-themed PS5 controllers last week, it was a safe bet that there'd be scalpers, store errors, and other disruptions in abundance — and that's exactly what happened when pre-orders opened this morning .

I got into a queue on PlayStation's online store half an hour before pre-orders began, and once the flood gates were opened, I was kicked to the back the line with an hour+ wait time. Thankfully, that time was quickly cut in half, likely from people unwilling to wait that long and leaving the queue, but even then, I still had issues. PlayStation's website kept giving me an error when I tried to sign into my account, forcing me to open the store in a new browser on another device. Eventually, I got through, but it was friction I could've done without.

So far, the controllers appear to be selling out at various retailers, though there is still some availability at the time of writing. GameStop and Best Buy are sold out of the white controller, while Target and Amazon appear to have them stock. Meanwhile, the black controller is exclusive to PlayStation Direct and appears to still be availabile.

PlayStation has implemented a system where users can only purchase one controller per account, which will likely limit some scalping, but not eradicate the issue. The controllers are currently being resold for nearly double the price on eBay, though it remains to be seen if people will actually buy them. It's unclear how long these controllers will remain in stock and if there will be a restock if they sell out.

With the release of pre-orders for the controller, we are just a little over two months away from the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Marketing is in full swing now, though it's unclear what will come next. Will there be another trailer for the game following the expansive, in-depth gameplay reveal ? Will Rockstar talk about GTA Online before release ? There are still a lot of questions, but at least we are in the endgame.

Grand Theft Auto 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Why Did PlayStation Ditch Kojima? Analysts Suggest Sony May Have Been 'Spooked' by Death Stranding 2 Sales
articles.summary: As the dust settles on PlayStation's announcement it's ditched a new game from Hideo Kojima, analysts are now discussing why Sony may have walked away.
articles.body:
As the dust settles on PlayStation's bombshell announcement that it has ditched Physint , an ambitious-sounding next-gen project from legendary Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima, analysts are now discussing why Sony may have walked away.

Physint will, of course, remain in production — though now backed by PlayStation's archrival Xbox, in a significant and much-needed PR win for Microsoft's gaming division.

Sony, meanwhile, is being seen as backtracking on yet another big public moment — this time, the enthusiastic handshake between PlayStation Studios boss Herman Hulst and Kojima that heralded Physint's announcement — even as fan complaints continue over PlayStation's disc-killing initiative, and disquiet over the shutdown of Destiny 2 development.

Why risk further backlash? For Dr. Serkan Toto, CEO of Japanese games industry consultancy firm Kantan Games, sales of Kojima's most recent title Death Stranding 2: On the Beach may be to blame.

"Kojima games have a strong platform marketing halo effect and are not about sales alone, but it seems the steep drop-off from DS1 to DS2 spooked Sony enough to cut him off," Toto wrote in a post on X/Twitter this morning.

Direct comparison between Death Stranding 1 and 2 is difficult as official sales for the latter were never announced by Sony or Kojima Productions "This is of course not a good sign," Toto noted, speaking to IGN.

Today, a fresh sales estimate from Alinea Analytics has pegged Death Stranding 2 at 2.5 million copies. This is a far cry from the number of players who tried the original Death Stranding — around 20 million, but there are caveats here.

Here's what we know for certain: that Death Stranding 1 had sold 5 million copies by March 2021, and had 20 million players by March 2025 — a figure that includes those who accessed the game via subscription services like Xbox Game Pass, or who claimed it free via Epic Game Store promotions. In July this year, Kojima Productions stated that the Death Stranding franchise had reached a cumulative 27 million players across both games.

Sales analysis, again from Alinea, suggests that Death Stranding 2 sales have now slowed to a trickle, that several notable discounts on the game have failed to move the needle, and that revenue for the game remains lower than that of its predecessor.

The picture that emerges here is one of a sequel that failed to build upon or even match the sales and reach established by Death Stranding 1. Perhaps this was enough to "spook" Sony, as Toto suggested, especially as both projects feel like lavish productions, with lengthy development cycles and Hollywood stars in key roles.

Looking ahead to Physint, it's possible Sony felt that the juice needed to fund a similar production scale and length was simply not worth the squeeze — especially as Physint looks to be even more ambitious, with yet more famous actors involved. Last year, Kojima estimated the game was still 5-6 years from completion , and there have been teases that some form of movie production is also involved .

All of these issues will now be Microsoft's to solve, though as Toto noted, the financial costs involved will be balanced somewhat by the positive impact this news has for Xbox as a brand, especially after a summer of layoffs, studio closures, and its own set of project cancelations to focus on games more likely to move the needle. While Physint may still be half a decade away, it is now a marquee title (and potential console exclusive) for Xbox's next-gen Project Helix.

"This doesn’t look great for PlayStation among core gamers," noted Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliot today. "Especially right now. From a strictly financial perspective, though, I can understand Sony’s position. In a vacuum, anyway.

"Ballpark math: word on the street is that the first Death Stranding cost about $100 million to make, and the second somewhere in the $150 million – $200 million ballpark (longer dev cycle, COVID, and all that)," he continued. "Depending on marketing overhead and the opportunity cost of pulling those Guerrilla developers onto DS1, the franchise has almost certainly broken even – but not by much.

"Margins are the name of the game now," Elliot added, suggesting that recent key misses from PlayStation Studios have made the company more cautious over which big-budget projects it backs. "Over the past few years, scares like Concord (cancelled, $300 million+ down the drain) and softer sales from the likes of Marathon (1.8M sold), Saros ($61M), Marvel Tokon (725K, $49M), and Lego Horizon Adventures (under 250K across Steam and PS5, $11M) seem to be making PlayStation more wary."

But while ditching Kojima will likely save many further millions, the optics of losing such a prestige project are uncomfortable at best, especially after the recent online ruptions over Bungie and physical media. "The PR miss of Xbox scoring off Sony’s stumbles could have been avoided," Elliot noted. And, as The Game Business' Christopher Dring noted on X/Twitter today: "You don't sign a Kojima game for the profit margin. It's a credibility play. Strong win for Xbox."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: The Paper Creators Say if The Office Was The Beatles, the Spin-Off Is Wings
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview, creators Greg Daniels and Michael Koman explain how The Paper Season 2 pushes past its roots in The Office with wilder stunts.
articles.body:
Season 2 of The Paper is now streaming on Peacock.

In Season 2 of The Paper, the Toledo, Ohio-set spin-off of the American version of The Office, the sitcom sheds some of its Dunder Mifflin baggage. Although similarities between the two series remain (Oscar’s still there, judging every harebrained scheme and social faux pas), The Paper’s new batch of episodes points to a show that’s working hard to come into its own. Simmering relationships are sped up, office gossip takes a spicier tone, and the fictional documentary crew tries some new tricks.

I sat down for an exclusive interview with series co-creators and executive producers Greg Daniels (King of the Hill, Parks and Recreation) and Michael Koman (Nathan for You) ahead of Season 2’s premiere, where they broke down some of the show’s key moments and revealed a series of very deliberate decisions that went into pushing The Paper beyond the confines of The Office.

How Ned and Mare Are “Very Different” from The Office’s Jim and Pam

From the very beginning of Season 2, main characters Ned (The Toledo Truth Teller’s editor-in-chief, played by Domhnall Gleeson) and Mare (Ned’s right hand and star reporter, played by Chelsea Frei) hit the gas on their romance that had been bubbling since Season 1. Daniels and Koman say that, while there will always be inevitable comparisons to The Office’s Jim and Pam, The Paper’s shorter seasons mean everything gets compressed.

IGN: The spine of the show this season is the relationship between Ned and Mare. I think a lot of folks would say, "Oh, they're the Jim and Pam of The Paper." But you guys very much push past that yearning and longing that Jim and Pam went through for so many seasons. Why did you decide to move forward with the central relationship so much more quickly in this show?

Greg Daniels: Well, you never want to repeat the same stuff that's been done before. And that starts with the fact that they're very different characters. But then also I think the genre's different. This is 10 episodes every year dropped at once. And we've been thinking of it a little bit more like books in a book series than a weekly year-long serialized story. So this was Book 2 for us with the relationship. I think it's probably unrealistic to think that we're going to get 100 episodes to tell the story, so we [sped] it up.

With The Paper living on a streaming platform instead of linear TV, both Daniels and Koman say that they feel more liberated in crafting dialogue that’s more grounded in real-world office conversations. While the results are often humorous, the rationale actually goes deeper, as evidenced by a scene between Oscar (Oscar Nuñez) and Detrick (Melvin Gregg) midway through the season where the two characters discuss a potential love interest for Oscar.

IGN: I wouldn't deem the show risqué, but you guys definitely push it a little further in this new batch of episodes. There's some cursing, there's some blue humor in there. Is it one of the benefits of being on streaming as opposed to network TV?

Michael Koman: Well, you still have to abide by certain rules because you get a rating. So you try not to drift into TV-MA. This is a show that we would like a whole family to be able to watch. [But] you want the show to sound real. So in a certain way, when language gets too sanitized, it starts to stop sounding real.

It feels different, television to streaming. And so I do think that there is this feeling that we should push a little bit. I think it's more of an instinct than some real intellectual thought. But there's just this sense of like, “Well, maybe we could make this conversation sound just a little closer to how we really talk.”

Daniels: What I think you're probably talking about is the cock block conversation.

Koman: Oscar and Detrick were having an important conversation about “cock blocking.” But for me, Oscar is actually talking about safe sex. In a way, it was wrong to bleep a conversation where a person is actually advocating for safe sex, no matter what language they're using because what they're saying is actually good for people.

If The Office Was The Beatles, The Paper Is Wings

While the show shares a fictional universe with The Office, Daniels and Korman say that the characters currently in rotation dictate ongoing storylines, not blind adherence to what came before.

IGN: The show still exists in the world of The Office. There were some overt callbacks in the first season. With Season 2, was that more challenging to further differentiate it from what became before?

Daniels: You write for the cast that you have and the characters that you've created, and you can almost forget that Oscar was on the other show. I don't really think that we're thinking about the original too much other than if somebody pitches a funny idea and we realize it's too close to something that's already happened on the original. But I don't really feel like there's this enormous pressure to connect the two worlds.

Koman: I will say, the last thing we ever do is intentionally make a connection where one character in our show is doing something that's in any way meant to echo something that happened on the other show. I think if anything, it’s a Beatles / Wings thing. Yes, occasionally some things are going to sound like the Beatles.

As the core staff of the Toledo Truth Teller continues to gel, a few new faces drop by this season to throw a wrench into ongoing storylines. New head of HR Lisa (played by Lisa Gilroy) stirs up incredibly inappropriate trouble the moment she shows up on screen. Likewise, Mare’s new colleague Todd (Jon Lovitz) crashes The Paper with a heavy dose of grouchy cynicism.

IGN: This season we see the addition of Lisa Gilroy as the new outspoken, borderline offensive, HR representative. Why did you decide to bring that character into the world?

Koman : We had thought about that character at the beginning of the season as somebody who was going to be very young, 19 years old or something like that. That was all we really had in our mind about what this character would be, and that she was in charge of HR and just was inappropriate, almost out of not knowing any better. And then when Lisa came up, it just seemed like, “Oh, well, that's the funniest possible person we could get to play the role.” She gives you a half an hour of options for a two-minute scene. I always think of Fred Willard and Catherine O'Hara as just the top of the mountain for improv. And to me, it was like that.

IGN: Jon Lovitz is a big part of this season. Were you guys thinking about him for this role? Did you write the part for him?

Daniels: I worked with him on Saturday Night Live, and I think he is an amazing actor. His work on A League of Their Own is so great. We were trying to think of some other journalistic types that you would find in a newsroom. And we had this idea of a very negative person, a sort of an Eeyore kind of reporter. And we had written it into the script as a John Lovitz type. And then we were like, "Well, wait a minute, maybe we could actually get Jon Lovitz to play the John Lovitz type! He'd probably be really good at playing a John Lovitz type!" And he just crushed it. So satisfying.

Esmeralda Has a Backstory, and It’s Hilariously Tragic

While new characters abound in Season 2, Daniels and Koman promise that some long-held questions about core characters do indeed have answers. For instance, Esmerelda, the Truth Teller’s narcissistic, vivacious, very Italian managing editor, played by Sabrina Impacciatore.

IGN: Why is Esmeralda in Toledo? Are we going to find the answer to that question? Is that somewhere where you guys have an episode dedicated to her backstory?

Daniels: We are talking about getting into her backstory more. We're sort of talking about what to do with her. But our backstory is that she was in a small town in Italy. An American came in, kind of swept her off her feet, promised her a very big time life in America. She left her little town basically with the attitude of, "So long, suckers." And then

Koman: She burned every bridge she had in Italy. There's no going back.

Daniels: There's no going back. And then he left her with a baby and now she's a single mom who can't go home and has made a pretty good life for herself until Ned shows up.

Daniels and Koman also made a deliberate attempt to make The Paper bigger in Season 2. Key moments include a tornado bearing down on Toledo, leading reporters Travis (Eric Rahill) and Adelola (Gbemisola Ikumelo) to seek shelter in a roadside ditch, and Mare and Ned spending a weekend away together, which is interrupted by cameras mounted on robotic food carts.

IGN: Maybe the biggest scene of the entire season is the scene in the ditch with the tornado.

Daniels: I knew you were going to say that! We love that scene. We protected it. It's so funny. That was part of the reason to do a tornado episode.

Koman: Ultimately, that image really made us laugh and we wanted to see it. I think that when you're making this kind of show, there is a point where you're looking at the resources that are being expended on this and feeling like I really hope this is worth it. There are cranes and pulleys involved and after all of that. But I mean, for my personal enjoyment, I felt like it was worth every penny.

IGN: On the opposite side of the spectrum was the food delivery cart camera. You had to be inventive to get that in there.

Daniels: The documentarian is a little bit morally compromised in that episode because he is kind of peeping into their hotel room. So we went back and forth a lot with the network about that because they were worried that we were going to make the documentarian a creep. We're very strict with the rules of the camera. And I think one of the things that always bugs me certainly is when you're on a supposed mockumentary and there's scenes in a bedroom and you're like, "Okay, wait a minute. Are they really going to do that with the cameraman there?" So we try to take that into account and it led to something funny.

IGN: I await Season 3 where you guys have Flock cameras recording.

Daniels: Flock cam, dashboard cam. There's a lot of cams everywhere.

For more on The Paper, read our Season 2 review and find out why we said the show continues to be a refreshing comedy and a worthwhile successor to The Office .

articles.title: Dead or Alive 6 Last Round Project Manager Sparks Debate After Revealing Koei Tecmo is Dialing Back the Game's 'Sexy Costumes'
articles.summary: Dead or Alive 6 Last Round Project Manager Tsuyoshi Iuchi has sparked a debate within the fighting game community after explaining why the team at Koei Tecmo is dialing back on making sexy costumes.
articles.body:
Dead or Alive 6 Last Round Project Manager Tsuyoshi Iuchi has sparked a debate within the fighting game community after explaining why the team at Koei Tecmo is dialing back on making sexy costumes.

Dead or Alive is a fighting game franchise with a fiercely loyal fanbase and a dedicated competitive scene. Despite these factors, it’s also known as the fighting game series with the most fanservice — a label that’s hard to get away from, given the jiggle physics, dating-sim-heavy spinoff games, and sexy outfits that exist in abundance in almost every DoA title.

While Dead or Alive 7 is in active development, DoA 6 Last Round is still getting content, including a new character that was just announced yesterday. Minato’s addition to the roster hasn’t come without controversy; some fans are accusing the schoolgirl of being a copy/paste of Honoka, while others are pointing toward a September 9 Famitsu interview that included some divisive remarks from the game’s development team.

Of these remarks, one is standing out from the rest: Project Manager Tsuyoshi Iuchi confirmed that Koei Tecmo is making the decision to step back from making more sexy outfits for Dead or Alive’s characters. This is a big change for the franchise, and one that’s been met with backlash and confusion from its fanbase.

The reason for this, Iuchi says, is because players are "embarrassed" to use such costumes when playing competitively. (This isn’t a huge surprise; swimsuit-style costumes for female characters have been banned or restricted at numerous esports tournaments across several different fighting games over the years.)

“I understand that some people are hoping for sexy costumes, but actually, sexy costumes tend to be used less frequently in competitive games due to embarrassment and other factors. For example, even in ranked matches, you don't often see your opponents wearing swimsuit costumes, right? This time, we're aiming for costumes that ‘people who like that character will continue to use,’ so the sexy elements are naturally kept to a minimum,” he said.

That’s not the only comment that’s catching players’ eyes; Director Akihiro Nakamura also responded to Famitsu’s question regarding Minato’s moveset, which the outlet noted was strikingly similar to Honoka’s.

“While they both use the same techniques, the key difference lies in their backstory: Honoka has an innate ability to instantly imitate any technique she sees, while Minato learns by studying through a device and through hard work,” he explained. “Additionally, Honoka enjoys watching martial arts and professional wrestling, so she chooses techniques she likes as a hobby, whereas Minato learns techniques with the visual appeal and enjoyment of dance in mind.”

This answer, combined with team's decision to slow down on sexy costumes, has left the DoA community equal parts frustrated and disappointed, leading to a wave of backlash from players online.

“What did we expect?” one fan wrote on X. “They don't care about the fans or the game. They want to shake a couple of more dollars out of the community with bare-minimum effort. I can already see DOA7 not having crossplay or rollback [netcode] and Koei saying, ‘$80 bucks, please.’”

“What happens when Minato fights Honoka? Is she going to steal her stolen moves, too?” prominent community member Emery Reigns said .

Even Japanese players aren’t happy with Minato’s moveset, with one writing , "Another cash grab? I shelled out for 6, but I can barely carry anything over, can't even change my hair color let alone power up — it's actually worse off, isn't it? Way too disappointing.”
