articles.title: Brandon Sanderson Praises the Upcoming MTG Star Trek Set for a 'Perfect Kirk' Card
articles.body:
Brandon Sanderson, author of the beloved Cosmere series , has long been a fan of Star Trek and Magic the Gathering. These are topics he has talked about frequently over the years, but thanks to the upcoming MTG Star Trek crossover, he got to talk about both things at the same time.

Sanderson and his co-host, Dan Wells, kicked off this week's podcast by discussing a few of the new cards being released this November. In particular, Sanderson pointed out the mono red Captain James T. Kirk card featuring what they agreed was "a perfect Kirk".

"I thought their Kirk was really clever," said Sanderson about the card. "If you have no options, he gives you them, right? He draws you a card and/or you discard a card and then draw one. So if you have no cards in hand, he gives you a card. So he solves the unsolvable problems, he makes a red shirt, and he buffs your team with a rousing speech."

The specific card Sanderson is talking about here is one of multiple versions of William Shatner's portrayal of James T. Kirk from the original series . It's a card you can pull from the base set, as opposed to one of the Commander Decks up for preorder. The MTG Star Trek sets aren't releasing until later in November, so it's unclear how common of a card this will be right now.

As for why Brandon Sanderson is talking about it on his podcast this week, we can only speculate. It could be that he just loves Star Trek and Magic the Gathering and wanted to spend some time talking about it. However, his penchant for tabletop adaptations and obvious interest in Magic the Gathering would suggest something more. This is perhaps just another sign that a Universes Beyond collab is in the works for Sanderson's sprawling Cosmere books.

This isn't exactly a new theory, as fans have been convinced that Sanderson's MTG collab is all but inevitable for a while now. Outside of his own personal interest, Sanderson showcased his ongoing relationship with Wizards of the Coast when he exclusively previewed a new card for Tarkir Dragonstorm back in March 2025. There's also been some discussion on Reddit about how he actually already created a custom Stormlight Archive set.

With the upcoming Apple TV adaptation in the works and massive new Stormlight board game on its way to Kickstart later this year, I certainly wouldn't rule out an MTG crossover like this in the future.

articles.title: Hasbro Responds to DHS Using AI Optimus Prime in Deportation Posts
articles.body:
Hasbro has responded to the Department of Homeland Security’s recent AI-generated social media posts that used the likeness of the Hasbro-owned character, Transformers’ Optimus Prime , to promote its deportation program, stating that DHS’ posts were created without their consent.

One DHS ad is an AI-generated fake movie poster for “Transformers: Age of Deportation” featuring Optimus Prime with DHS and ICE insignia.

A second DHS post showed Optimus face to face with a Sikh man, declaring, “Self-deport or find out” and “America for Americans. Get off our roads; you don’t know how to drive Mr Singh.” That post – which the DHS has since deleted – was widely blasted as being blatantly racist.

Hasbro responded Thursday with the following statement on their Instagram account :

“Optimus Prime is a beloved character who represents humility, leadership, compassion and justice. Hasbro is aware of the recent posts using his likeness. These posts were done without permission and do not represent the Transformers brand or Hasbro.”

As Entertainment Weekly points out, the DHS’ Optimus Prime spots were also criticized for coming on the heels of the death of Peter Cullen , the actor who voiced Optimus for decades.

Cullen’s final performance as the iconic Autobot leader will be in Optimus Prime: Awakening, an upcoming short film that will be presented with 40th anniversary screenings of The Transformers: The Movie .

The Trump Administration widely uses (often AI-generated) imagery and videos that appropriate pop culture in their social media posts.

The DHS’ Optimus Prime posts come on the heels of the White House’s AI video featuring President Trump as a Green Lantern and the release of the designs for new Space Force uniforms that have been likened to those worn by the Galactic Empire in the Star Wars franchise or by the soldiers in Starship Troopers, a sci-fi film that lampoons fascism.

articles.title: The Retroid Pocket Duo Looks Perfect for DS and 3DS Emulation
articles.summary: It’s no secret that handheld gaming is in a bit of a renaissance right now. Ushered in by the Nintendo Switch and carried forward by the Steam Deck. Alongside these mainstream offerings are another class of handhelds aimed more at the past than the future. In particular, Android-powered dual-screen handhelds like the new Retroid Pocket Duo look to offer hardware designed for emulating the Nintendo DS and 3DS.
articles.body:
It’s no secret that handheld gaming is in a bit of a renaissance right now. Ushered in by the Nintendo Switch and carried forward by the Steam Deck and more powerful handheld PCs like the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ , there’s never been more options for playing games on the small screen, whether that’s away from home or just around the house without being tied to a console.

Alongside these mainstream offerings are another class of handhelds aimed more at the past than the future. In particular, Android-powered dual-screen handhelds like the AYN Thor look to offer hardware designed for emulating the Nintendo DS and 3DS. This week, Retroid entered the fray teasing out its upcoming Pocket Duo, and today we now know how much it will cost.

The Retroid Pocket Duo will cost $270 for the flagship model, which comes with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, though there’s a coupon to knock $20 off when pre-ordering. There’s also a cheaper Pocket Duo Lite model with half as much RAM and storage, which will cost $150. Both models come in a variety of colors, including ones reminiscent of GameCube purple, Game Boy greyish-white, and clear blue and atomic purple. Pre-orders are currently sold out.

The Pocket Duo offers a 5.5-inch 1080p AMOLED primary screen, while the second screen is 4.5 inches at 960p. It’s powered by a Qualcomm Dragonwing Q-7790 processor and runs Android 16, which offers a plethora of games via the Play Store, as well as multiple options for DS, 3DS and other retro system emulation. If going this route, games should be obtained legally, such as by dumping your own game cartridges – IGN does not condone piracy under any circumstances.

There’s no word yet when the Pocket Duo and Duo Lite will launch, but these prices make it an excellent alternative to the AYN Thor, which offers a less-powerful Snapdragon 865 in its $259 Lite model, while the Thor’s “Base” model moves up to the more powerful Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 for $329. Pre-orders are currently sold out, but these handhelds tend to come available in waves, so keep an eye out for future drops if you’re interested in buying one. In the meantime, we’ll be looking to go hands-on with the Pocket Duo, so stay tuned for our review as we get closer to launch.

articles.title: The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset With Infinite Battery Life Drops to $250
articles.summary: Wireless free with zero downtime.
articles.body:
One of the best wireless gaming headsets is on sale today. Both Amazon and Best Buy currently have the Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro wireless gaming headset for Xbox, PS5, and PC for just $249.99 with free shipping, a savings of $100 off the retail price. Note that although this is specifically the Xbox model, it also works with the PlayStation console. SteelSeries released a successor - the Nova Pro Omni - earlier this year, but it currently sells for $380 and the improvements are certainly not worth the $130 price premium.

SteelSeries Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset for $250

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset (Xbox, PS5, PC)

The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro has long been one of IGN's highest rated wireless gaming headsets . IGN's Kevin Lee gave the Nova Pro a 10/10 "Masterpiece" review and I believe it still holds today. I've clocked well over a thousand hours on mine to the point that my earcups were worn through (I replaced them with the awesome WC Freeze gel earpads ). I now use the Arctis Nova Omni and I will be honest with you, I can't really tell the difference, probably because I use my headset almost exclusively for PC, and the Omni's pièce de résistance is its seamless cross-platform switching. If your use-case is similar to mine where you predominantly use these headphones for one platform, then stick with the Nova Pros.

The one feature that undoubtedly makes the Nova Pro stand out amongst the crowd is the ingenious hot-swappable battery system . The Nova Pro includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your headset and the other to remain charged and ready to go in a base station that doubles as a charger. This way, you get wireless freedom with zero downtime . Each battery lasts for up to 22 hours of continued use so you don't need to swap out too often.

The base station deserves additional mention. Not only does it charge your battery, it also features a clear and legible OLED display and a handy volume control knob. On the rear are USB inputs for connecting to your PC as well as an optional 3.5mm passthrough should you want to connect your speakers directly to the base station.

Of course a high end gaming headset is no good if it can't produce great sound and deliver vocal clarity. The Nova Pro is first and foremost a gaming headset, and it delivers big sound with its big 40mm neodymium dynamic drivers and 360° spatial sound effects (via SteelSeries Sonar for PC, Tempest 3D Audio for PS5, and Microsoft Spatial Sound for Xbox). The retractable boom mic is clear without any static and does a great job of canceling out ambient noise. My friends regularly point out that I sound like I'm in a quiet room because they hear nothing but my voice.

The Nova Pro is comfortable to use even during gaming marathons thanks to the suspension-style headband and comfortable leatherette ear cushions. You don't have to worry about babying it either, since the headband has a steel inner core. I've tossed mine around more times than I should have and it's still functionally perfect.

articles.title: Lady Dimitrescu Actor Maggie Robertson Would Say Yes in a Heartbeat if Capcom Called to Reprise Her Breakout Resident Evil Role
articles.summary: Maggie Robertson has said she would accept any opportunity from Capcom to reprise her breakout role as Lady Dimitrescu in the Resident Evil series, calling the character her “firstborn.”
articles.body:
Maggie Robertson has said she would accept any opportunity from Capcom to reprise her breakout role as Lady Dimitrescu in the Resident Evil series, calling the character her “firstborn.”

Lady Dimitrescu, the towering face of Capcom’s phenomenally successful 2021 game, Resident Evil Village , was Robertson’s first video game role, and it changed her life forever.

Speaking to IGN at gamescom while promoting her latest video game gig — the sultry and scheming Tasha in upcoming Dungeons & Dragons game Warlock , Robertson said the last five years had been a surreal experience.

“That game, that character changed my life in every way,” she said. “There's no aspect of my life that has not been touched by that character. That was the very first game I ever did. And I had just done my graduate degree. I just came from a drama program. I lived the Hollywood dream in a surreal way. So I just graduated, moved to LA January 2019 and was throwing paint at the wall. I didn't have an agent. I was just self-submitting for things, seeing what stuck. I moved out here to pursue on-camera predominantly, but then this breakdown happened across my path and it was a day where I was just feeling like I might as well try something new. F**k it. Let's go for it. And it turned out to be this.”

Robertson said she had no idea which game or character she was auditioning for when she went in for Lady Dimitrescu, due to the secrecy that surrounds the video game industry, and even afterwards, could never have predicted the impact it would have.

“Video games also are always under NDA. So everything about the breakdown, the character names, the sides that I auditioned with, all of that was fake,” she said. “I had no idea what I was even auditioning for. I had no idea of the scope of what video games could offer me in terms of a career, in terms of acting, in terms of the roles that I would have access to.”

Resident Evil Village: The Evolution of Lady Dimitrescu and Her Daughters

Such was the online popularity of Lady Dimitrescu following the character’s reveal ahead of Resident Evil Village’s release, that Capcom thrust her into the forefront of the game’s marketing. Lady Dimitrescu appeared on billboard advertising, in viral social media posts, and was in pretty much every Resident Evil Village trailer as Capcom doubled down on the vociferous fandom that emerged around the character.

Fast forward five years, and Robertson has acted in everything from Baldur’s Gate 3 (Orin the Red), to Fortnite (DJ PJ). In Warlock, Robertson plays another Dungeons & Dragons villain, Tasha, patron to the playable character. Such is Robertson’s fame within the video game industry that she appeared on-stage at Opening Night Live last month to introduce Warlock gameplay. And there are more video game roles to come.

“Ultimately, I'm so grateful for it because I think my type with theater, my type with on-camera, the roles that I am so right for are roles that are waiting for me when I am 50 and 60 years old,” she continued. “And I didn't have access to those at the time that I was entering the industry. And being able to become a part of this industry helped me have access to those roles now. And I didn't have to wait. I didn't have to be limited by the way that I looked. Again, it's like, if you imagine yourself, if you can imagine it, you can be it. And I find that so liberating.

“But that is the Hollywood dream. That is what they sell you, is that you never know when your big break is going to happen. You never know what opportunity is going to be your next big break. And that happened to me. I just said yes on a random thing.”

The big question for Resident Evil fans is whether Lady Dimitrescu might appear in another game in the series, or perhaps in an animation or maybe even in live-action. Capcom has yet to say either way, but Robertson would jump at the chance.

“Oh, of course!” she said. “A hundred times, yes. She's my firstborn. So anytime they call, I will say happy days.”

For now, though, the focus is on Warlock and her character, Tasha. "What I like most about Tasha is that she's neither good nor evil," Robertson said. "She's complex in that way. She can go either way depending on the day. I think that gives you a lot of fun to play with. She's so charming and charismatic, but also cunning, and is ultimately looking after number one, which is herself. And she'll help you for sure, but there's always something in it for her if she decides to help you. And you don't always know what that is. So I found her to be a nicely complex character. I always like getting to work on those."

articles.title: 'I Really Want Game Pass to Work' — After Navigating the Xbox 'Reset,' Double Fine Boss Tim Schafer Is Indie Once Again
articles.summary: After navigating the Xbox "Reset," Double Fine boss Tim Schafer is indie once again. IGN interviewed the developer on what happens next.
articles.body:
It's only been a few months since developer Double Fine's split from Microsoft, but the team behind Psychonauts 2 , Kiln , and Keeper is looking ahead. With another successful Kickstarter campaign under its belt, the newly independent studio's second (or should that be third?) life as an indie is off to an optimistic start. With the current Kickstarter focusing on the developer's latest Amenesia Fortnight — a developer-run game jam where new micro games are produced — it's allowing the developers to build up some much-needed runway as they plan for their next major project.

At PAX West 2026, we spoke with Double Fine studio head and president, Tim Schafer, about the developer's current path forward. Along with talking about his return to independence following the biggest restructure in Xbox history , Schafer reflected on Double Fine's years under Microsoft's banner, and explained how Game Pass can still potentially work as a subscription service. He also reaffirmed his commitment to making Brutal Legend 2 (provided someone can front the money for it).

IGN: It's been seven years since the Microsoft acquisition, and the game industry has gone through so much change. What's it been like to return to being an independent developer?

Tim Schafer: It's been exhilarating. Like, it's scary because we've got to make our own way in the world, but we did that for 19 years before Microsoft, so we have a lot of great ideas and a lot of experience pitching them. A lot of people know it's a tough time out there. A lot of people, and now especially a lot of the older developers, are gone. A lot of the old avenues we used for funding are gone, but there are a lot of new ones. So we're just putting ourselves out there, meeting a lot of new people, and talking about who wants to make games with us.

IGN: I think what's been great to see with Double Fine is that it has a core audience of players that are invested in seeing the studio thrive. I remember the original Kickstarter campaign for Broken Age was a big breakthrough for Double Fine.

Schafer: Yeah, I mean that sort of thing was quite like a big financial impact, but it was also an awakening of just how tight we are with the community, like how dependent we are on them, and how much they're willing to participate. You know what I mean? Because they participate financially, but also creatively. Like, they really want to make art as well. I feel like that's something special about our fans, and it's because our number one thing is creativity. So I think it breeds a fan who also likes creativity, and I think it, hopefully, helps our games inspire not just players, but people to like learning to draw or program, or, you know, people who want to know how to make a game.

IGN: Now that you are an independent developer again, and with all this attention on you, do you feel there's a certain responsibility placed on you all to make it as an indie studio?

Schafer: I don't see it as a responsibility. I mean, I don't expect anybody to look at us and know what to do, because our situation always feels really unique to Double Fine and me. Like we're an indie game studio, but we have a lot of employees, and we have healthcare, and we have a lot of stuff like that. There's not a lot of companies our size anymore, like AA-size studios, kind of. So, I wouldn't say do everything that we do. I hope no one's following our example because I don't know if it works for anyone but us.

IGN: The Kickstarter for the Amnesia Fortnight is an interesting way to start this comeback, it's all about this big push to produce some new ideas and bring to life.

Schafer: It's kind of like a celebration of what we can do now that was harder to do before. Even being at PAX, Microsoft usually likes to have one big booth. So having little booths all over is not what they're into. They're not even here at the show. So being independent, we can come to PAX, we can talk to the fans, we can set the prices of our games. We can do tiny games like Thank You Bus Driver, which is a new project for us, and we made a whole special label for them called Double Fine Action Labs, where we can release smaller ideas, do game jams, and do the kind of things we like to do. So it's a celebration of both what we can do and what we like to do, which is high-bandwidth interaction with the fans, doing silly creative things, and just having a lot of fun.

IGN: I would be remiss not to say that a lot of people took notice of the Kickstarter mentioning that Brutal Legend 2 can be made if you secure $100 million. I understand it was meant as a joke…

Schafer: I mean, it was a joke, but also, it's not a joke. Sure, I mean, if we got $100 million, we would do it for sure. I would happily put everything aside and make Brutal Legend 2, as long as I could talk Jack Black into it. Yeah, but if we got $100 million, that's great. Yeah, I could do a demo for $100 [ laughs ]. But it's not a joke — I would do it if we hit that goal. We're probably not going to hit that, though. But any rich guys out there, if you ever want to see Brutal Legend 2, come help us out.

IGN: Now that you're back as an independent developer, how do you feel about those seven years working under Microsoft? Would you say that it was a valuable experience in the end?

Schafer: I learned a lot from it, and it was a really great experience overall. They invested a lot in the company, and their mission was to support Game Pass and other projects. So for a while, we were very closely aligned, and it was great. It was a great partnership, and then their goals changed, and so we parted ways because of that.

But I feel like, in the meantime, we had a great little collection of studios within Xbox Game Studios, like Compulsion, Ninja Theory, Obsidian, and inXile. We got to meet all the studio heads and talk to them, and our programmers got to talk. Their programmers are artists, and everyone was exchanging ideas and technology, and it was really a great learning experience about how other companies are run. So, because you're independent, you're a little more like an island. So, being an island that was temporarily pushed, hitched up to a bunch of other islands was very much, "Oh, that's a cool game right there, we could go play that game."

IGN: Game Pass was such a big part of the Xbox brand's push for a larger games audience. Do you feel that Game Pass still has value and potential as a service?

Schafer: I really want Game Pass to work. I like the idea of subscription models for companies like us, who, you know, lower the barrier to entry for everyone. We want to make games that are weird and creative, that you might not understand at first. I think that's the kind of stuff we like to do. Do people see the key art and go like, "What?" And if it's on a subscription, you've already kind of paid for the game. You'd be more likely to try it, so that sounds good.

But there are other ways to reach people like that, like lowering your prices, for example. You know, getting people to try your games like that. I think it could have worked. I don't understand why Netflix worked and Game Pass didn't, and I think that's something I just don't know enough about, but that's the way it is. So now we're taking another approach: making it really affordable.

IGN: It's been interesting to see the rise of these micro-games, ones that are fairly modest in concept, but offer variety and fun for groups of players. I know the term "friendslop" is used a lot, but I kind of see some of Double Fine's games, and experimental ones, being right at home with those styles of games – particularly Kiln.

Schafer: Yeah, I think the difference is multiplayer. We have built a ton of multiplayer, but the thing about those games kind of aligns with what we're doing with our Amnesia Fortnight, which is just trying stuff. A lot of those games came from game jams. I think the game Peak came from a game jam, and we just want to give everyone in the company a chance. Really, people feel safe to experiment and try creative ideas, and then to not spend $300 million on them, just spend like sticky bus drivers for six weeks, put it out there, and just see what you know.

The thing about those 'friendslop' games, people mostly focus on successes, but there's tons of them that don't work out. I think the idea is that you never know which one's going to take off, so don't bank the future of your company on any one individual idea for sure. But these games were called "friendjank" for awhile, you remember that? It's also about casual pacing, it's basically games where it's mostly about hanging out with your friends.

IGN: What are your thoughts on the state of the industry now? There's been a lot of reports and stories of developers struggling to stay open and some creatives having to leave the field. Do you feel optimistic that things can improve?

Schafer: It's a shitty time out there, and it's been getting worse for longer than I've ever seen it get worse. I usually try to comfort people by saying to the team, "Well, there are cycles, there are downturns, but it always turns back up again because you need people to make games, and that comes and goes." But this has been going on for at least four years, and I feel like I've never seen a cycle plunge so low.

Is it a permanent change in just the economics of it all? But people are still needed to make games. It's not like AI has replaced everybody, and for all the talk about it replacing Google, it's not effectively replacing anybody right now. So where are all those jobs going? I still see a bunch of games getting made, and people are still needed. So I wish I were smarter and knew the answer to that. But it seems like you need people to make games, and so there should be a ton of opportunities, and they're still making a lot of money.

For creatives, you have to have fun making games because they're really hard to make. A lot of these people could make more than money in a tech company, so they're here because they love games. And if you're here because you love games, then you should love what you're doing, love making games, and have fun.

articles.title: Woot Has a Grade A Refurbished Nintendo Switch 2 Available for $449, Though Not for Long
articles.summary: Woot has a Grade A refurbished Nintendo Switch 2 available for $449 for a limited time. Compared to paying full price for a brand new console now post-price hike, you're saving $50 through this offer.
articles.body:
Woot (an online retailer owned and operated by Amazon) has a Grade A refurbished Nintendo Switch 2 console available to buy right now for $449, which is $50 cheaper than the console's brand new list price of $499.99 after the recent price hike . If you don't mind buying a refurbished model, it's quite a nice offer to take advantage of, especially if you're hoping to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake in November or explore the game deals in the upcoming Switch sale .

Nintendo Switch 2 Console (Grade A Refurbished)

This console offer won't be around for long, though. Woot's store page says that there's just 15 days left to take advantage of it, or it's available until it's sold out, which could happen at any point. So, if you're really hoping to grab it, now is your chance.

And if you're curious what exactly 'Grade A Refurbished' means, Woot's store page says: "This item has been inspected and guaranteed to have minimal cosmetic damage & has successfully passed a full diagnostic test which ensures like-new functionality & removal of any prior-user's personal information." It also adds that, "Unit includes OEM accessories and is packaged in a generic white or brown box."

Before the console's recent price increase kicked in, we did spot this same console offer at Woot for $399.99 , but that was also a $50 difference in cost compared to the Switch 2's previous full price of $449.99. So overall, this remains quite a nice offer to jump on for a refurbished model. Again, it won't be around for long, and we may not see a console offer like it until Black Friday or Cyber Monday , so this is as good a time as any to grab it.

If you're hoping to find even more Nintendo deals, make sure to mark your calendar for the upcoming 'Customer Appreciation' sale , which starts on September 13 and runs through September 26. This will include 30% off Switch games and much more, so it'll be worth having a look at. Especially if you pick up this console, it'll be a great time to grab some new games for your library.

articles.title: The Amazing Spider-Man #1000 Preview Teases a Bleak Fate for Aunt May
articles.summary: Marvel has released a new preview for The Amazing Spider-Man #1000, one which teases a huge new tragedy in Peter Parker's life.
articles.body:
The Amazing Spider-Man #1000 is shaping up to be the biggest comic book release of September, if not the whole of 2026. This is the first time an ongoing Marvel series has legitimately reached the issue #1000 milestone, and Marvel is going all-out with a massive lineup of creators and new stories . But now, all eyes are on the main story from writer Joe Kelly and artist Pepe Larraz. Is Peter Parker about to face his worst nightmare?

That certainly seems like a distinct possibility in light of a new preview for this tale. Building on the cliffhanger ending from The Amazing Spider-Man #35, this story explores the fallout of Aunt May suffering a major stroke. Check out our updated preview gallery below to see more:

The Amazing Spider-Man #1000 Preview Gallery

Marvel's press release teases, "Destined to take its place in comic book history, the epic milestone issue marks a major turning point in Joe Kelly and Pepe Larraz’s acclaimed run with a pulse-pounding lead story that delivers the shocking fate of Aunt May and sets the stage for a revelatory showdown with the all-new super villain Ravage."

Will Aunt May actually die in this issue? It wouldn't be the first time Marvel has flirted with killing off the most important woman in Peter's life. May previously "died" in 1995's The Amazing Spider-Man #400, but it was later revealed that this was an actress hired by Norman Osborn to mess with Peter's mind. May was also on death's door in 2007's Spider-Man: One More Day storyline, which ended with Peter making the hugely controversial choice to sacrifice his marriage with Mary Jane to Mephisto in exchange for healing May. Has May been living on borrowed time ever since?

However, this preview suggests a potentially different outcome. We can see that Peter arrives at the hospital just in time for May to awaken, only to discover she doesn't recognize him. It seems her stroke caused major brain damage and memory loss. While she could well suffer another, fatal stroke in this issue, it's also possible that Marvel is establishing a new status quo where May simply doesn't remember her favorite nephew. That would be its own form of emotional torment for Peter.

The Amazing Spider-Man #1000 will be released on September 30. Check back with IGN then for a full breakdown of the big developments in this issue. Marvel will also release a second printing of the issue on October 28, with new sketch variant editions of Larraz and John Romita, Jr.'s covers.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .
